title: Retry Auto-Configure OBS can start OBS streaming without a live control channel, so teardown may leave OBS streaming at a dead room
test: tests/browser/host-obs-control-channel.spec.mjs: 'Retry Auto-Configure OBS opens a control channel that pagehide stops OBS through' (failed before); 'a control channel that never opened does not stand in the way of the stopObsStream fallback' and 'a Retry that ends after Stop Sharing opens no control channel' (regression guards for the other two sentences of VAL-091; they passed before, see the proof)
proof: Holds. The spec starts its own server.js with WHIP on (the shared Playwright server has it off, and the host view only configures OBS once the WHIP endpoint is ready) and stands in for OBS with page.routeWebSocket on ws://127.0.0.1:4455: a stateful obs-websocket v5 stub that answers the handshake and GetStreamStatus/StartStream/StopStream/SetStreamServiceSettings, and that can refuse connections like a closed OBS. Case (2) of the issue: OBS refuses everything for the start, so its configure and its control channel both fail (the alert shows and the Retry button appears); OBS is then brought up and Retry clicked, and the status reads 'OBS configured'. On the unchanged client (built to a scratch dir, served by the lane's server.js on claimed ports) the first test failed: 'open OBS connections after the retry' Expected 1 Received 0, i.e. the retry's configure connection had ended and no control channel was left, so a pagehide teardown had nothing to write the stop frame to. After the fix the same step sees exactly one open connection, and a dispatched pagehide puts StopStream on that very connection and opens no new one. Fix: the Retry handler takes the session's operation (startGuardRef.current.activeOperation) at click time; in the configure .then it does nothing when that operation is no longer current (Stop, a room that ended, unmount or pagehide), otherwise sets the status as before and calls establishObsControlChannel(retryOp), the same helper the start uses, whatever result.success says. The helper (TASK-063) already opens a channel only for a current operation and drops (and closes) a channel whose ready reports failure when the ref still points to it, so the ready-failure step needed no change. The second test (start against a refusing OBS, then Stop Sharing opens one fresh connection to OBS, the stopObsStream fallback, instead of handing the stop to the dead channel) and the third (Stop Sharing while the retry's SetStreamServiceSettings is held; the retry then runs to its end and leaves no open connection and opens none) passed on the unchanged client, since TASK-063 had already made the helper clear a failed channel and the retry opened none at all. Mutation check: removing the helper's isCurrent line, the retry's isCurrent line and the ref-clearing on ready failure makes the second test fail (Expected 3 Received 2) and the third fail (a live connection left, Expected length 0 Received 1). Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (751/751); the spec was run with a private Playwright config (no web server) while holding the Playwright lock, 3 of 3 pass.
